solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Astonishing attention shown by Bishop Wareing, ultimately leering at nurses (4-8)

indicators.note: to be shown by something is to appear beside it, so MIND stands next to B
ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter of Wareing
to nurse is to hold close, as a baby in the arms, so OGLING holds the G

blocks.note: the last letter of WareinG, placed inside OGLING

annotation.surface: A bishop called Wareing has been caught leering at the nurses, which is astonishing behaviour.
annotation.walkthrough: The shocking bishop is only there to supply a B and a G; 'nurses' looks like hospital staff but is the verb, holding something close.
annotation.definitionFit: Something mind-boggling is so astonishing the mind cannot take it in.

entries.clue: Author to a greater degree pens story (7)

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in, as sheep in a pen, so MORE shuts LIE inside

blocks.note: a story = a lie, as in 'don't tell stories'

annotation.surface: An author outdoes himself by writing even more stories.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like what an author does with a story, and it means encloses.
annotation.definitionFit: Molière was the French comic playwright, author of Tartuffe.

entries.clue: Loonies in plot foolishly skirting universal environmental problem (5,9)

indicators.note: letters arranged foolishly are out of their sensible order, i.e. rearranged
to skirt is to go round the edge of something, so the anagram goes round U

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters, rearranged as NOISEPOLLTION

annotation.surface: A gang of loonies hatching a foolish plot around some worldwide environmental problem.
annotation.walkthrough: The U has to sit inside the rearranged letters rather than beside them; 'skirting' is what says the anagram goes round it.
annotation.definitionFit: Noise pollution is excessive man-made noise, treated as damage to the environment.

entries.clue: One pursuing punch up involving hot takeaway dish? (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' reads the word from bottom to top
to involve is to wrap up or enfold, so BAJ enfolds H in its middle
to pursue is to follow behind, so I comes after the rest

blocks.note: a jab is a quick punch; turned up it gives BAJ
H = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Someone after a fight, involving something spicy from the takeaway.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the dish is only one example of a takeaway. A bhaji is an Indian fritter, usually onion, a staple of British curry-house menus.
annotation.definitionFit: A bhaji is a spiced fried vegetable fritter sold in Indian takeaways.

entries.clue: Composer, singer who mostly improvised (8)

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so WHO loses its last letter
something improvised is made up afresh, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A composer and a singer who made most of it up as they went along.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits a list in the surface, but 'Composer' alone is the definition and 'singer' is plain fodder. Improvisation suits a jazz-inflected composer.
annotation.definitionFit: George Gershwin composed Rhapsody in Blue and Porgy and Bess.

entries.clue: Customer saving skin, right? (4)

indicators.note: 'saving' in its old sense of except: the word without its skin, its outer letters

annotation.surface: A shopper asks whether they are entitled to protect their skin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saving skin' reads like skincare, but 'saving' is the old sense of except, so the customer loses its outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to hold someone's property until a debt is paid.

entries.clue: Miser pinches rolls round here intermittently (9)

indicators.note: what rolls tumbles over into a new position, so the letters of PINCHES are rearranged
round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round EE
intermittently means at intervals, so take every other letter of 'here'

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of hErE

annotation.surface: A miser helps himself to bread rolls on his rounds here and there.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pinches rolls' paints a miser stealing bread, but 'pinches' is the fodder and 'rolls' the instruction. The answer is an old word for a skinflint, originally a ship's purser.
annotation.definitionFit: A nipcheese is a stingy person, one who would pare even the cheese.

entries.clue: One way to end up below Arsenal? (10,4)

definitions.text: One way to end up below Arsenal?

blocks.clueFragment: One way to end up below
blocks.note: the surface means finishing lower in a league table; the setter means a route that takes you underground, beneath a place
not the football club but the London Underground station named after it

annotation.surface: A football supporter fearing their side will finish the season beneath Arsenal in the league.
annotation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London Underground station; riding the Tube line through it is a way to end up underneath it. The football reading of 'end up below' is the decoy.
annotation.definitionFit: The Piccadilly line is the Tube line that runs through Arsenal station.

entries.clue: Novelist initially attending party, being picked up after 02:00 (6)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of 'attending'
in a down clue, lifting DO turns it upside down
'after' in its sense of later in sequence: OD follows TWO in the answer

blocks.note: a do is a party; turned upwards it gives OD

annotation.surface: A novelist leaves a party and is collected by car in the small hours.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as a lift home, but in a down clue it turns the party upside down; the time is not a digit string to parse but just a number word.
annotation.definitionFit: Margaret Atwood is the Canadian novelist of The Handmaid's Tale.

entries.clue: Adult in pound store ejecting English dog (5)

indicators.note: 'in' in its sense of inside: A sits within the other letters, between L and IKA
to eject is to throw out, so the store throws out its E

blocks.note: L = pound, from the Latin libra (£)
A = adult, the old film certificate
IKEA, the furniture store, without E for English

annotation.surface: An adult in a pound shop throws out an English dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pound store' reads as a single shop (a pound store sells everything for £1), but it is two pieces: L and a store.
annotation.definitionFit: Laika was the Soviet dog sent into orbit on Sputnik 2 in 1957.

entries.clue: Rope peer into dancing, including foxtrot (4,5)

indicators.note: letters that dance move about into a new order
to include is to take something in as part of the whole, so F joins the letters being rearranged

blocks.note: Foxtrot = F in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Look into ballroom dancing, the foxtrot included.
annotation.walkthrough: The foxtrot sits naturally among 'dancing', but here it is only the radio code word for F.
annotation.definitionFit: A reef point is a short rope on a sail used to tie in a reef.

entries.clue: View affirmation cardinal welcomes (8)

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them inside, so EIGHT opens up to hold YES

blocks.note: a cardinal number, as opposed to an ordinal

annotation.surface: A view on affirmation that a cardinal of the church is happy to welcome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it means a cardinal number.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, one's view.

entries.clue: Crazy Horse enters wide circle (6)

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so HACK goes in between W and O

blocks.note: a hack is a riding horse

annotation.surface: Crazy Horse, the Sioux chief, rides into a wide circle.
annotation.walkthrough: Crazy Horse was a Lakota war leader, so the two words look inseparable; split them into definition and wordplay. A wide in cricket is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach.
annotation.definitionFit: A slangy, informal synonym: someone whacko has gone off their head.

entries.clue: Mother feeding deadheaded plant raises quality of Narcissus (8)

indicators.note: to feed is to put something in, so MA goes into the plant
a deadheaded flower has lost its head, so the plant loses its first letter

annotation.surface: A mother feeds and deadheads a plant to bring out the best in her narcissus.
annotation.walkthrough: The gardening surface makes Narcissus look like the flower; with a capital N it is the Greek youth who fell in love with his reflection.
annotation.definitionFit: Narcissus was consumed by self-love, and egomania is obsessive self-regard.

entries.clue: Inventor of unintroduced brand fitting in speech (9)

indicators.note: a word without its introduction has lost its first letter, so MARK becomes ARK
in speech means as spoken, so RIGHT is heard, and written as WRIGHT

blocks.note: MARK (a brand) without its first letter

annotation.surface: An inventor of a brand of fittings that nobody introduced properly.
annotation.walkthrough: The inventor is Richard Arkwright, whose water frame for spinning cotton helped start the Industrial Revolution.
annotation.definitionFit: Arkwright was the 18th-century inventor of the water frame.

entries.clue: United defeated, gutted when crushed by blow (6)

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving D…D
something crushed by another is squeezed inside it, so DD sits within WEED

blocks.note: blow is slang for cannabis, as is weed

annotation.surface: A football report: United lost, the team gutted and crushed by the blow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'United defeated, gutted' reads as a Manchester United result; 'United' is actually the definition and 'blow' is drug slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Wedded means joined together, united in marriage.

entries.clue: On reflection, can old indulged animals hurry? (4,2,2)

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the whole string is read backwards

annotation.surface: Pondering whether old pampered animals are able to get a move on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb in the question but is a noun, a tin; the three pieces are built first and then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Step on it' is an order to hurry, as in pressing the accelerator.

entries.clue: Hound half of graduates lapped by runner (6)

indicators.note: take the first half of ALUMNI
to lap is to wrap or fold round, so SKI is wrapped round ALU

blocks.note: a ski is a runner, as on a sledge

annotation.surface: A pack of graduates is hounded by a runner who laps them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete lapping the field; here it is the runner of a sledge.
annotation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender Middle Eastern hunting hound.

entries.clue: Writing self-contained epitaph needs time (6)

blocks.note: RIP, rest in peace, the standard epitaph

annotation.surface: Writing a compact epitaph takes time.
annotation.walkthrough: SC is the British estate-agent abbreviation for a self-contained flat, one with its own kitchen and bathroom.
annotation.definitionFit: Script is handwriting, or written text generally.

entries.clue: Catching echo, paces across middle of Wesleyan churches (8)

definitions.note: Steeples are the towers of churches; the clue uses the part for the whole.

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so STEPS holds E
to lie across something is to span it, so the steps span LE, enclosing it
take the central letters of Wesleyan

blocks.note: Echo = E in the NATO alphabet
the two central letters of wesLEyan

annotation.surface: Pacing about a Methodist church, listening to the echo.
annotation.walkthrough: The echo and the Wesleyan chapel both fit the church scene, but neither is doing churchy work: one is a radio code letter and the other just gives its middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Steeples stand for churches, by the part for the whole.

entries.clue: Cast entertaining unknown new clubs in timely agreement? (7)

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so SHED holds Y, N and C

blocks.note: to cast, as a snake casts its skin, is to shed

annotation.surface: A cast of actors taking on an unknown new crew of clubs, all in agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a theatre company but is the verb. The question mark flags the playful definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Things synched happen together in time, in timely agreement.

entries.clue: Report on short walk (6)

blocks.note: a turn = a stroll, a brief walk

annotation.surface: A report about going for a brief stroll.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the official kind of report, such as a tax form or election results.
annotation.definitionFit: A return is a formal report, like a tax return.

entries.clue: Devil always takes register before operating (8)

indicators.note: to take is to take in, receive, so AY receives POLL inside it
'before' in its sense of earlier in sequence: that string comes ahead of ON

blocks.note: ay (or aye) = always, an old word
a poll is a register of voters

annotation.surface: The devil is always signing up before he starts work.
annotation.walkthrough: AY for always is archaic ('for ay'). The answer is the destroying angel of Revelation and the fiend Christian fights in Pilgrim's Progress.
annotation.definitionFit: Apollyon is a name for the Devil, the Destroyer of the Book of Revelation.

entries.clue: Rabies checked by mounting embassy legislation (5)

indicators.note: to be checked by is to be held back inside, so the answer is held in the words that follow
mounting means climbing, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards

annotation.surface: An outbreak of rabies held back by ever more embassy regulations.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the old medical name for rabies, from the Greek for frenzy.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical synonym: lyssa, Greek for frenzy, is the old clinical term for the disease.

entries.clue: Fish alone (4)

blocks.note: a flatfish, and the commonest crossword fish of four letters
alone as in only or single: the one and only

annotation.walkthrough: Two definitions side by side with nothing in between: the sole is a flatfish, and sole also means only.
annotation.definitionFit: The sole is a flatfish, and sole also means only or alone.

entries.clue: Ruminant wicked husband — but not wife — kept in filth (9)

indicators.note: 'but not' excludes something, so W is removed from the letters
what is kept in is held inside, so the result sits within PORN

blocks.note: WRONG + H, then W taken out

annotation.surface: A wicked husband, minus his wife, is kept in the gutter with his vices.
annotation.walkthrough: H = husband and W = wife are standard genealogy abbreviations; the dashes fence off the deletion.
annotation.definitionFit: The pronghorn is a North American antelope-like animal that chews the cud.

entries.clue: Cane son roughly when drinking whiskey (5)

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so S and ISH take W inside, as if swallowing it

blocks.note: Whiskey = W in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A father canes his son roughly when the boy is caught drinking whiskey.
annotation.walkthrough: The Victorian punishment scene hides that 'Cane' is the definition, a verb, rather than the start of the story.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to cane someone is to beat them with a stick, and a swish is the stroke of the cane through the air.

entries.clue: Superior Theresa, fantastic in role (7,5)

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful, out of the ordinary, so the letters of THERESA are rearranged
'in' in its sense of inside: the anagram goes within STEAD

blocks.note: stead = place, role, as in 'in his stead'

annotation.surface: A mother superior called Theresa gives a fantastic performance in a role.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Superior Theresa' reads as a Mother Superior; 'Superior' is the definition, and 'in role' puts the anagram inside the word for role.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: to be streets ahead is to be far superior, a long way in front.
